newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ireland says IRA truce needed for talks.
newsitem.headline: Ireland says IRA truce needed for talks.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring insisted on Tuesday that the Irish Republican Army (IRA) restore a ceasefire before its political wing, Sinn Fein, can be allowed to take part in Northern Ireland peace talks.
Spring addressed the U.N. General Assembly one day after British security forces seized a large quantity of explosives and arms, saying they had foiled an imminent IRA bomb attack in Britain.

Sinn Fein has been excluded from political talks on the future of Northern Ireland, sponsored by the British and Irish governments, because the IRA broke its 17-month ceasefire in February with a series of bomb attacks in London.
The IRA is fighting to end British rule in the province.

"Political dialogue is only sustainable and productive on the basis of the principles of democracy and nonviolence," Spring said. "That is why there must be an unequivocal restoration of the IRA ceasefire before Sinn Fein can enter the negotiations."

He said negotiations including all parties were the best hope of achieving a durable settlement to the conflict in Northern Ireland, which has lasted for more than 25 years and claimed at least 3,000 lives.
A suspect was killed on Monday during the British police raids, which confused further an already complex picture about whether the IRA is ready to renew its ceasefire.

Irish Prime Minister John Bruton prompted new optimism about the peace process on a trip to the United States two weeks ago, suggesting a new truce might be at hand. British and Irish media, quoting security sources, backed his assessment.

But media reports said it could be preceded by a final "big bang" by the IRA just to prove to London that it was operating from a position of strength. Those favouring unity with Ireland moved quickly to douse the speculation, saying the reports were groundless.
Britain also says Sinn Fein will not be given a seat in multiparty political talks while the IRA wages war.
